prompt.text_prompt: A cinematic fairy-tale royal garden plaza at the gates of an extravagant pastel castle city, rendered at high-end animated-film quality, bright warm daylight. FOREGROUND: a wide plaza of pale cream and soft grey CHECKERED FLAGSTONE, worn and mossy in the joints, scattered with fallen pink and violet petals. LEFT: a tall ornate GOLD gate with dense filigree scrollwork, curled volutes and heart-shaped finials, hung between pale carved stone piers wrapped in ivy and climbing roses; beside it a round red-and-white playing-card sign bearing a heart. RIGHT: an enormous gnarled tree with deeply furrowed bark rising out of frame, an ornate gold-rimmed CLOCK FACE set into its trunk and an oval gilt PORTRAIT FRAME hanging from it, curtains of wisteria and ivy trailing down through it. MIDGROUND: a rose-covered stone ARCHWAY over shallow steps leading deeper into the garden; hedges clipped into a giant HEART shape studded with pink roses; a colossal porcelain TEACUP painted with hearts, sitting on stacked saucers, with a matching teapot nearby; GIANT MUSHROOMS in clusters — scarlet caps with white spots, deep violet caps, and pale cream ones — among dense beds of pink, violet and white flowers, foxgloves and hydrangeas. BACKGROUND: a dense fantasy castle city of slender WHITE AND CREAM STONE towers with conical roofs in ROSE PINK, MAGENTA, LILAC and pale blue, gold finials and small pennants, mushroom-domed turrets, tier upon tier receding into soft lavender atmospheric haze. SKY: bright blue-to-lavender with soft white and pink clouds; ornate GOLD KEYS and a white porcelain TEAPOT float weightlessly in the air. MATERIALS: glossy glazed porcelain, polished gold leaf, carved pale limestone, painted timber, moss, wet stone. Extremely high geometric density, every surface detailed and intentional, strong foreground-to-distance depth, volumetric light through the arch. NO characters, NO people, NO animals, NO dogs, NO creatures of any kind — the garden is empty of living figures. No bare ground, no untextured blocks, no repeated primitive shapes, no modern objects, no lettering or readable text.

source_reference.kind: founder-reference-image, cropped above the dog band
source_reference.why: The first generation (47928d7e) reproduced the Relay Dogs from the reference despite an explicit NO-DOGS text prompt — image conditioning beat the negative. Cropping above the dog band removes the input that caused it, which is more reliable than asking the model again not to. It also matches the architecture: Marble is the BACKDROP and the plaza the dogs stand on is authored Unreal geometry, so the cropped-away region is exactly the region Marble should not be supplying.

assets.caption: The scene is a cinematic fairy-tale royal garden plaza at the gates of an extravagant pastel castle city, rendered at high-end animated-film quality, with a bright, warm daylight illuminating the fantastical environment. The overall tone is enchanting and whimsical, inviting exploration into a meticulously crafted dreamscape. The plaza, a wide expanse of pale cream and soft grey checkered flagstone, shows signs of elegant age with worn, mossy joints and scattered pink and violet petals. A tall, ornate gold gate with dense filigree scrollwork, curled volutes, and heart-shaped finials, is hung between pale carved stone piers wrapped in ivy and climbing roses, with a round red-and-white playing-card sign bearing a heart beside it. An enormous gnarled tree with deeply furrowed bark rises from the plaza, an ornate gold-rimmed clock face set into its trunk and an oval gilt portrait frame hanging from it, while curtains of wisteria and ivy trail down its massive form. A rose-covered stone archway extends over shallow steps, leading deeper into the garden, while hedges clipped into a giant heart shape are studded with pink roses. A colossal porcelain teacup, painted with hearts and sitting on stacked saucers, is placed near a matching teapot, creating a playful focal point. Giant mushrooms in clusters—scarlet caps with white spots, deep violet caps, and pale cream ones—emerge from dense beds of pink, violet, and white flowers, including foxgloves and hydrangeas. The backdrop is a dense fantasy castle city of slender white and cream stone towers with conical roofs in rose pink, magenta, lilac, and pale blue, adorned with gold finials and small pennants, and complemented by mushroom-domed turrets, tier upon tier receding into a soft lavender atmospheric haze. The sky is bright blue-to-lavender, featuring soft white and pink clouds, with ornate gold keys and a white porcelain teapot floating weightlessly in the air. The materials used throughout—glossy glazed porcelain, polished gold leaf, carved pale limestone, painted timber, moss, and wet stone—contribute to an extremely high geometric density, where every surface is detailed and intentional, creating a strong foreground-to-distance depth and volumetric light filtering through the arch.

hq_mesh_url.note: Downloaded directly onto the Lightning box, not through fetch(): 141 MB and the import happens there. The signed URL needs no auth, so the API key never left the control machine. On the box the file is a symlink into wonderland/marble-assets/ so the 471 MB of mesh lives outside the repo.

transform.axis_note: glTF is Y-up right-handed; Unreal is Z-up left-handed. Interchange applies the conversion on import; unreal_rotation_deg is the ARTISTIC yaw on top of it.

backdrop_policy.parallax_rule: A player who steps w metres shifts a feature at depth D by atan(w/D). Past about 3 degrees a single-viewpoint shell visibly smears, because it cannot reveal what was hidden from the viewpoint it was reconstructed from. At NATIVE scale that allows only 1.7 m of movement before the nearest tenth of the geometry breaks, which is not an open world.
backdrop_policy.the_lever: SCALE THE SHELL UP AND PUSH IT OUT. Parallax error falls linearly with distance and the imagery subtends the same angle, so a shell scaled by k looks identical from the arrival point and tolerates k times the movement. It stops being a place and becomes a very large dome, which is what a backdrop is.
backdrop_policy.authored_ownership: Authored Unreal geometry owns everything inside the roam radius and provides ALL ground the player stands on. The shell provides nothing walkable and carries no collision. Where they overlap, the authored plaza occludes the shell's near geometry — which is the cheap alternative to culling it.

transform.anchor_camera_source: hero_shots[0] in wonderland/infra/build/generate-hub-level.py — ARRIVAL_HERO, the shot the world opens on
transform.origin_why: The mesh origin is the reconstruction viewpoint, so the actor origin goes ON the arrival camera. Every ray from HeroCam0 is then unchanged by the uniform scale, which is what makes the 6x backdrop lever free.
transform.scale_convention: MEASURED IN THE ENGINE, not assumed. UE 5.8's glTF import already applies the metre-to-centimetre conversion: the mesh arrives at 100 uu per glTF unit. The first import proved it — a 96.979-unit span came in at 9,697.9 uu. So the ACTOR scale is the metric factor itself (2.1145), times the backdrop multiplier (6) for a backdrop; it is NOT that times 100. Both scales here were 100x too large and the import measured 12,303,954 cm against an expected 123,039 — a 123-kilometre shell.
transform.scale_measured_at: 2026-08-22, first live import, UE 5.8 container dev-5.8
transform.axis_correction_why:
ROLL 180, and the note that used to sit in source_mesh.axis_note said the opposite. That note reasoned: the raw vertex data is Z-up, the single node carries a +90-degree X rotation presenting it as glTF Y-up, so no manual correction is needed. The premise is right and the conclusion is backwards. R_x(+90) maps +Z to MINUS Y — the canonical Z-up-to-Y-up export rotation is R_x(MINUS 90) — so the node rotation CREATES the Y-down convention instead of cancelling it, and UE's Y-up-to-Z-up conversion then lands the world's up on UE -Z.
Three independent confirmations. (1) The quaternion, recomputed: raw +Z goes to glTF (0,-1,0). (2) This world's OWN collider export carries no node rotation and its Y runs -58.200..+0.716 — the huge-negative, tiny-positive signature of Y-down, the same one the sibling royal-garden world measured and corrected with this same [180,0,0]. (3) The first live import measured extents in RAW axis order (x,y,z), which only happens if the node rotation was applied, giving UE Z = -raw Z.
Without this the shell imports UPSIDE DOWN: ground plane above the camera and a kilometre of castle city hanging below the plaza. Every gate stays green — one actor placed, level saved, clean cook — because check_scale compares SORTED extents on purpose, so that an axis swap is not mistaken for a size error, and a 180-degree flip changes no extent.
transform.axis_correction_open_question: A 180-degree roll restores UP and also negates UE Y, which swaps what is in front of the arrival camera with what is behind it. That is a proper rotation, not a mirror, and it is what the sibling world measured — but whether the castle city ends up ahead of HeroCam0 or behind it CANNOT be settled from the file. The first capture settles it. If the city is behind, add transform.unreal_rotation_deg = [0,0,180]; that field already exists for exactly this and needs no import-logic change.

collision_source.detail: Marble geometry is imported NoCollision. Gameplay collision and navigation stay native Unreal — see MARBLE.md.

source_mesh.measured_from: glTF accessor POSITION min/max in the GLB JSON chunk
source_mesh.unlit_note: The export is KHR_materials_unlit: its lighting is BAKED INTO the texture. That is what a backdrop wants. If UE's importer drops the extension the mesh becomes lit and Wonderland's sun re-lights an already-lit texture — check the material after the first import rather than assuming either way.
source_mesh.axis_note: CORRECTED 2026-08-22. The raw vertex data is Z-UP (Z runs -0.94 to +80.5 while X and Y spread horizontally) and the single node carries a +90-degree X rotation. The earlier note concluded from this that no axis correction was needed. That was wrong: R_x(+90) sends +Z to -Y, so the node rotation puts the world's up on glTF -Y and UE lands it on -Z. See transform.axis_correction_why.

texture.note: 8192 is exactly UE's default maximum texture dimension, so it imports without being downsized. Block-compressed it is about 43 MiB of VRAM with mips — nothing on a 23 GB L4.

source_mesh.double_sided_risk: THE MOST LIKELY WAY THIS IMPORT LOOKS LIKE A FAILURE WHILE REPORTING SUCCESS. The material is doubleSided, which matters because a single-viewpoint reconstruction is a shell VIEWED FROM INSIDE: if UE imports it single-sided and the winding faces outward, every gate here passes — one actor placed, right size, level saved, cook clean — and the frame shows nothing. If the backdrop is missing from the capture, check the material's Two Sided flag before touching placement.
